remaining.quote: Buyers navigate three distinct stages from initial planning to closing day.

Start with the [Home Buying Checklist](/checklists/home-buying-checklist/) to manage 59 financing and purchase tasks, or evaluate loan limits with our [home affordability calculator](/mortgage/home-affordability-calculator/).

During your inspection window, use the 62 checks on the [Home Inspection Checklist](/checklists/home-inspection-checklist/) to examine physical systems, then complete the 30 verification steps on the [Final Walkthrough Checklist](/checklists/final-walkthrough-checklist/) before signing closing papers.
Sellers follow an organized process to prepare a residence, market the listing, and coordinate required transfer documents.
The [Home Selling Checklist](/checklists/home-selling-checklist/) draws from a 44-item library to help schedule pre-listing maintenance, staging requirements, and closing disclosures.
Tenants and property owners use dedicated tools tailored to leasing decisions and daily management.

The [Rental Checklist for Renters](/checklists/renting-checklist/) contains 53 items for lease reviews, while first-time renters can use the 42 items on the [First Apartment Checklist](/checklists/first-apartment-checklist/) alongside our [renting vs buying comparison](/compare/renting-vs-buying/).

Document property turnover room by room with the [Move-In / Move-Out Condition Checklist](/checklists/move-in-move-out-checklist/), which creates 36 items for a studio or 89 items for a three-bedroom house, and apply the 45-item [Landlord Checklist](/checklists/landlord-checklist/) for lease compliance.
Property owners managing tenants can select the dedicated landlord checklist to oversee leasing and maintenance.
Yes, the landlord checklist provides 45 operational tasks designed specifically for property owners and managers.

The items draw from published federal guidance by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and American Society of Home Inspectors (ASHI).
